scientific_question: Can a three-parameter Gaussian trained on central wavelengths predict both the low- and high-wavelength tails of the independent Eckerle4 transmittance data?

data.name: NIST/ITL StRD Eckerle4
data.reference: Eckerle, K., NIST (1979), Circular Interference Transmittance Study
data.units_as_published: y is transmittance; x is wavelength; no unit conversion or measurement uncertainty is invented

model.optimizer: scipy.optimize.curve_fit with identical settings and two starts; select the lowest training residual sum of squares

holdout_rule.purpose: Independent two-tail extrapolation; no random interpolation, no selection of the easier tail

full_fit_certification_rule.purpose: Separate known-answer reproduction against NIST, never used as holdout evidence

baselines: Ordinary least-squares linear response fitted only on the middle training interval
metrics: Middle training RMSE, low-tail RMSE and high-tail RMSE
Pooled holdout RMSE, MAE and maximum absolute residual
Each tail compared with its corresponding linear-baseline RMSE

decision_gate.limited_support: Pooled holdout RMSE < 3 * middle training RMSE AND pooled holdout RMSE < pooled linear-baseline RMSE AND each tail RMSE < its linear-baseline RMSE
decision_gate.negative_or_unresolved: Otherwise report the model class as not supported for this two-tail task; no retuning or tail selection after seeing residuals
decision_gate.interpretation: Passing is limited evidence for this single dataset and split only, not a universal Gaussian law, proof of independent replication or parameter endogeneity

output_rule: Write validation/eckerle4-two-tail.json and papers/06_第二真实数据外推/fig06_eckerle4_two_tail.png; preserve all starts and negative results; refuse to overwrite existing results
prohibitions: No fitting or parameter selection on any of the eight tail observations
No replacing the two-tail protocol with high-tail-only or low-tail-only after seeing results
No claim that NIST certification is our independent experimental replication
No claim that fitting proves a universal Gaussian law or all parameters are physically endogenous
